record_type_quote: In this replication and extension study, we tested an alternative explanation for their results: the tasks with social information also provided spatial information which could explain improved performance. In a study with 278 college students, we used the two versions of the tasks from their study (no social or spatial information and with social and spatial information) and added two versions that isolate only social and only spatial information.

targets.outcome_quote: Our replication of Tarampi et al.'s analyses found no difference in females' performance on the tasks; however, when both females and males were included, we found some evidence for better performance in the social and spatial condition.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central claim was that social information uniquely improves female performance. The replication analyses found no female performance difference; pooled-sex evidence for combined spatial/social information does not confirm the original sex-specific claim. The authors attribute improvement to spatial cues instead.
